title: The meeting of Cortes and Motecuhzoma is told by both a Nahuatl tradition and Cortes's letter
summary: A Nahuatl-tradition account and Cortes's letter both describe the 1519 meeting, and they do not say the same thing.
body: Two documents opened here describe the same encounter from different sides. The Nahuatl-tradition text stages Motecuhzoma's greeting. Cortes's letter to Charles V describes the city and the ruler for a Spanish king. Neither text is a neutral minute. This card does not decide whether the greeting was submission, diplomacy, or a later literary shape. The wording on the page includes: "Cortés When Motecuhzoma [Montezuma] had given necklaces to each one, Cortés asked him: "Are you Motecuhzoma? Are you the king? Is it true that you are the king Motecuhzoma?" And the king said: "Yes, I am Motecuhzoma." Then he stood up to welcome Cortés; he came forward, bowed his head low and addressed him in these words: "Our lord, you are weary. The journey has". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording. A further page states: "to convey to your Majesty a just conception of the great extent of this noble city of Temixtitlan, and of the many rare and wonderful objects it contains; of the government and dominions of Moctezuma, the sovereign: of the religious rights and customs that prevail, and the order that exists in this as well as the other cities appertaining to his realm:".
